newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz sees double-digit growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Allianz sees double-digit growth in 1997.

text.p: German insurer Allianz AG Holding said on Wednesday it expected its earnings to grow at a double-digit rate in 1997 after pre-tax profit rose by a third in 1996.

In a preliminary report on 1996 earnings, the company also said that its net profit rose 10 percent to 2.2 billion marks. It said it would raise its 1996 dividend payout to 17 marks from 16 on its 1995 results.

"Barring any major claims or natural catastrophes and assuming that the capital markets will remain stable overall, Allianz projects that profits will show moderate double-digit growth this year," the insurance giant said in a statement.
A spokesman for the group added that this was the first time a large international insurance company had made a forecast of this kind at this stage in the year.
Allianz said its goal was to turn an underwriting profit in 1997, after narrowing its underwriting loss by some 500 million marks to 150 million marks in 1996.

The group also said its premium income would rise around 12 percent this year to 84 billion marks following its consolidation of health insurance unit Vereinte Holding and the consolidation over the full year of Hermes Kreditversicherungs credit insurance group and the Swiss Berner group.
"Excluding these changes, Allianz Group premium income worldwide would increase a projected four to five percent," the statement said.
Allianz's 1996 pre-tax profit figure was somewhat above expectations but its net figure was fully in line with average forecasts.
Allianz's after-tax profits had been expected to show a more modest increase than the pre-tax earnings because the comparative net figure for 1995 had been inflated by a tax break.
